channel.title: Guides to Pay, Age and Health in Korea | moatool
channel.description: Plain-English guides to working in Korea: take-home pay, severance, unemployment benefits, annual leave, weekly holiday pay, Korean age, and BMI.

item.title: Take-home pay in Korea: what is deducted
item.description: What comes out of a Korean salary: national pension, health and employment insurance, income tax, and rules for foreign workers such as the 19% flat tax.

item.title: How severance pay works in Korea
item.description: How Korean severance pay works: who is eligible, the official formula, how average wage is calculated, and when it must be paid.

item.title: Unemployment benefits in Korea for foreign workers
item.description: Who can get Korean unemployment benefits, including foreign workers by visa type, how the daily amount is calculated, and how many days it is paid.

item.title: Annual leave in Korea: days and unused leave pay
item.description: Paid annual leave under Korean labor law: 11 days in the first year, 15 after, up to 25, what happens after exactly one year, and unused leave pay.

item.title: Weekly holiday pay in Korea (juhyu sudang)
item.description: What juhyu sudang (weekly holiday pay) is, who gets it in Korea, how it is calculated for part-time work, and why a full-time monthly wage uses 209 hours.

item.title: Legal age in Korea and Korean age explained
item.description: What is the legal age in Korea? Adulthood is 19, voting 18, alcohol from January 1 of the year you turn 19. How Korean age works, with legal sources.

item.title: Korean vs WHO BMI categories
item.description: Why a BMI of 24 is normal under WHO categories but pre-obese in Korea. Compare the two scales and the research behind lower Asian cut-offs.
